scores.claim_text: FY2022 customer concentration: RTX 14%, U.S. Navy 14%, LMT 10%; defense/USG ~97% of revenues.
supports: usaspending(direct, recipient_name='Mercury Systems, Inc.', cutoff 2023-01-15): only 73 awards, $9.25M total — orders of magnitude smaller than implied by the 14%+14%+10% concentration claim (which implies ~$380M+ of revenue derives from these customers)
edgar_fts(RTX 0000101829, search='Mercury Systems', cutoff 2023-01-15): 0 hits — RTX's filings do not name Mercury Systems as a material supplier
edgar_fts(LMT 0000936468, search='Mercury Systems', cutoff 2023-01-15): 0 hits — LMT's filings do not name Mercury Systems either

Note: the broader usaspending search (recipient_name='Mercury Systems') returns 589 awards / $550M because it pulls in Physical Optics Corp (acquired Dec 2020) — but POC contracts are awarded TO PHYSICAL OPTICS, not Mercury directly
scores.M_value: MRCY-direct DoD awards through cutoff: $9.25M / 73 awards. RTX/LMT 10-K mentions of Mercury Systems: 0/0
scores.interpretation: The revenue concentration claim is structurally consistent with Mercury's subcontractor model (revenue flows through prime contracts, not direct DoD purchases — so direct USG awards being small is expected). However the orthogonal counterparty check fails: NEITHER RTX (14% customer) NOR LMT (10% customer) names Mercury Systems anywhere in their EDGAR full-text filings through the cutoff. That is a soft red flag for materiality on the prime side — if Mercury is ~$140M+ of RTX FY22 sourcing, it would normally appear in supplier-related disclosure. Scored MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY — the customer concentration claim isn't disproven, but the counterparty asymmetry suggests Mercury's importance to its primes is much smaller than the reverse exposure.

scores.claim_text: Rollup thesis: 15 acquisitions / $1.4B since FY14; FY22 revenue $988.2M of which $117.8M acquired.
supports: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence(parent_thesis=mission processing/RF/EW/secure microelectronics, 4 named recent deals): signal=INCOHERENT_ROLLUP, mean_coherence=0.0, n_low_coherence=4/4 (NOTE: LLM judge defaulted to low when descriptions lack rich context; signal direction is suggestive not conclusive)
12% of FY22 revenue ($117.8M / $988.2M) is acquired — high dependence on M&A to maintain growth

FY22 net income collapsed to $11.3M from $62.0M FY21 (-82%) despite higher revenue — classic rollup margin-compression signature: 15 deals, $1.4B deployed, $200.5M adj EBITDA = ~14.4% LTM EBITDA on $1.4B of deployed capital
Operating cash flow swung from +$97.2M (FY21) to -$18.9M (FY22)
scores.M_value: INCOHERENT_ROLLUP signal (with LLM-judge caveat); 12% of revenue acquired; net income -82% YoY; OCF negative
scores.interpretation: Independent of the J-Book pattern, the rollup narrative shows stress: aggregate $1.4B M&A spend has not produced commensurate adj-EBITDA growth ($200.5M FY22 vs $201.9M FY21 = flat YoY despite $117.8M of acquired revenue), net income collapsed 82%, OCF turned negative. The 1MPACT restructuring is itself an admission that prior M&A integration has been suboptimal. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY on the implicit growth-via-acquisition thesis. (Caveat: acq_coherence LLM 0-score reflects sparse input, not strong incoherence evidence — narrative scoring should be treated as ancillary.)

scores.claim_text: Substantial patent / IP portfolio underlying the Processing Platform.
supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee(Mercury Systems, cutoff 2023-01-15): n_total_applications=20, n_granted=7
For a company describing itself as having 'industry-leading' R&D investment >2x competitors on a percentage basis with FY22 revenue $988M, 7 granted patents is sparse
scores.interpretation: The IP-portfolio claim is light on substance: 7 issued patents against $988M revenue and a 40-year operating history is below comparable defense-tech peers. Not a fatal disclosure — Mercury operates an integrator/COTS model so much of the value is in trade secret / supply chain rather than patentable IP. Scored MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY rather than RED to reflect the integrator-model caveat.

summary.framework_note: J-Book verifier is structurally out-of-range for a 2023-01-15 cutoff: the FY26 corpus post-dates the cutoff, so all forward-funding queries return NOT_FOUND_IN_TIMERANGE or NOT_FOUND. The divergence pattern cannot be tested directly at this PIT. The strongest non-J-Book signals are: (i) counterparty-asymmetry — RTX (14% customer) and LMT (10% customer) do not name Mercury anywhere in EDGAR full text, suggesting Mercury's importance to its primes is smaller than the reverse exposure; (ii) rollup-thesis stress — $1.4B deployed across 15 deals has produced flat adj-EBITDA YoY, net income collapsed 82%, OCF turned negative, 1MPACT itself admits prior integration was suboptimal.
